decks.domain: Driving, right of way and sharing rules

cards.front: Complete the rule: Match speed to conditions, share the road courteously.
cards.back: Match speed to conditions, share the road courteously, and move only when safe and clear of traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Walk around a parked car before reversing, and.
cards.back: Walk around a parked car before reversing, and never reverse or halt in a travel lane; keep going to a safe pull-off.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Obey officers, flaggers, traffic devices and traffic.
cards.back: Obey officers, flaggers, traffic devices and traffic laws as the first rule of the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal one hundred feet before turning in town.
cards.back: Signal one hundred feet before turning in town and three hundred feet before turning on rural roads.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep right except to pass on roads with.
cards.back: Keep right except to pass on roads with three or more same-direction lanes, favoring the center lane amid entering traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a missed turn or forgotten signal, continue.
cards.back: After a missed turn or forgotten signal, continue to the next intersection, get in position, signal, then turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never drive on the shoulder.
cards.back: Never drive on the shoulder unless directed to do so.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Obey posted limits and drop below.
cards.back: Obey posted limits and drop below them for bad road or weather conditions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Interstates post seventy-five or eighty for cars and.
cards.back: Interstates post seventy-five or eighty for cars and light trucks by day and night, with heavy trucks held to sixty-five.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Urban-area highways post sixty-five for all listed vehicles.
cards.back: Urban-area highways post sixty-five for all listed vehicles day and night near Billings, Great Falls and Missoula.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Two-lane highways post seventy by day and sixty-five.
cards.back: Two-lane highways post seventy by day and sixty-five at night for cars and light trucks, with heavy trucks at sixty days and fifty-five nights.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A two-lane driver may exceed the limit by.
cards.back: A two-lane driver may exceed the limit by ten miles per hour while overtaking and returning safely right.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pass only when safe, using the left of.
cards.back: Pass only when safe, using the left of the centerline on two-lane roads and the leftmost lane on multi-lane roads.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Passing on the right is legal only past.
cards.back: Passing on the right is legal only past a left-turning vehicle or on wide multi-lane pavement, never off the roadway or on the shoulder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without turn controls, turn from the lane nearest.
cards.back: Without turn controls, turn from the lane nearest the destination side into the nearest lane of the new road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep right turns tight without swinging wide left.
cards.back: Keep right turns tight without swinging wide left first or finishing wide in the far lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid cutting left turns into approaching traffic.
cards.back: Avoid cutting left turns into approaching traffic while leaving room for oncoming left-turning vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn around only with five hundred feet of.
cards.back: Turn around only with five hundred feet of clear view both ways and no approaching vehicles, never on busy streets, curves or hills.

cards.front: Complete the rule: No turn is made unless the vehicle is.
cards.back: No turn is made unless the vehicle is in the proper lane and the move is safe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The law assigns yielding duty and grants no.
cards.back: The law assigns yielding duty and grants no absolute right-of-way, so every driver must act to avoid striking anyone.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white.
cards.back: Blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane hold absolute right-of-way; never sound the horn at them.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, yet no.
cards.back: Drivers yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, yet no pedestrian may step off the curb into a vehicle path.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Night walkers should wear light clothing or carry.
cards.back: Night walkers should wear light clothing or carry a light, and walking on the roadway is unlawful where sidewalks exist.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Roadway walkers keep left facing traffic, cross at.
cards.back: Roadway walkers keep left facing traffic, cross at intersections using provided crosswalks, and obey applicable traffic laws.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Passing left of the centerline is the two-lane.
cards.back: Passing left of the centerline is the two-lane norm, while passing on the right is limited to left-turning vehicles and wide multi-lane pavement.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Right-of-way is yielded under the rules, never seized.
cards.back: Right-of-way is yielded under the rules, never seized, and every driver must still act to avoid a crash.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Town turns need a one-hundred-foot signal and rural.
cards.back: Town turns need a one-hundred-foot signal and rural turns a three-hundred-foot signal, with the shoulder never a driving lane.

cards.back: Drivers crossing sidewalks or entering and leaving driveways, alleys and lots yield to pedestrians; sidewalk driving is illegal except to cross.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Right on red is allowed after stopping in.

decks.domain: Driving, right of way and sharing rules

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow down and watch for children near schools.
cards.back: Slow down and watch for children near schools day and night, checking speed on every approach.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A funeral procession means two or more vehicles.
cards.back: A funeral procession means two or more vehicles with lead and escort units, one carrying remains, traveling in daylight hours.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Outsiders yield to procession vehicles and must not.
cards.back: Outsiders yield to procession vehicles and must not split, join for advantage, pass on the right, or cross its path through red.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, after which.
cards.back: The lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, after which followers may proceed through with reasonable care for others.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Procession drivers follow closely, cap speed at fifty-five.
cards.back: Procession drivers follow closely, cap speed at fifty-five on fast highways and near the limit elsewhere, burn all lights, and flash signals together on first and last cars.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Procession drivers still yield to signaled emergency vehicles.
cards.back: Procession drivers still yield to signaled emergency vehicles and keep due regard for every road user.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Bicycles count as vehicles under the traffic laws.
cards.back: Bicycles count as vehicles under the traffic laws that reasonably fit, so motorists adjust for their slower travel when passing and sharing.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pass a cyclist as a slow vehicle by.
cards.back: Pass a cyclist as a slow vehicle by crossing the centerline with no oncoming traffic to leave a recommended five feet, or by slowing to the cyclist pace until passing is safe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Expect cyclists off the shoulder and often.
cards.back: Expect cyclists off the shoulder and often in single-file groups that need extra passing time.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Cyclists ride as far right as practical, often.
cards.back: Cyclists ride as far right as practical, often eighteen to twenty-four inches into the lane to deter unsafe in-lane passes.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Shared-lane arrow markings guide cyclist position and warn.
cards.back: Shared-lane arrow markings guide cyclist position and warn motorists to leave room, differing from bike-lane bicycle symbols.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Motorists grant cyclists full vehicle rights, never deliberately.
cards.back: Motorists grant cyclists full vehicle rights, never deliberately block them, pass only without endangering anyone, and yield inside designated bike lanes.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Cyclists ride single file except on exclusive paths.
cards.back: Cyclists ride single file except on exclusive paths, when passing another bike, two abreast on shoulders or parking lanes, or two abreast on multi-lane roads without extra impedance.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slower-than-traffic cyclists keep near the right edge except.
cards.back: Slower-than-traffic cyclists keep near the right edge except when passing, preparing a left turn, dodging hazards or narrow lanes, or avoiding parked-car doors.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Bicycles often lack mirrors, so drivers treat an.
cards.back: Bicycles often lack mirrors, so drivers treat an approached cyclist as unaware and proceed with extra care.

cards.front: Complete the rule: School bus stopping duties at railroad crossings.
cards.back: School bus stopping duties at railroad crossings are set by the cited state statute.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The funeral lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, while.
cards.back: The funeral lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, while followers behind it may proceed through with reasonable care.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Outsider drivers must not split or join a.
cards.back: Outsider drivers must not split or join a procession for advantage, while procession drivers follow closely without the usual spacing.
